purpose: Review the Batanes pole-held cast-net assessment as a coastal marine fishery source without treating its gear-limited catch composition as a full provincial checklist or current occurrence layer.

source.title: Pole-held Cast Net Fisheries in Batanes Province, Philippines
source.publication: Thalassas: An International Journal of Marine Sciences, volume 41, article 251 (2025)

studyScope.setting: Nearshore marine and reef-flat pole-held cast-net fishery; locally named nanaúy/nanawuy, using mayripid and ipayvuya gear variants.
studyScope.excludedMunicipality: Itbayat was excluded from the cast-net study; the article attributes this to the lack of tidal reef formations used by the gear.
studyScope.reportedStudyPeriod: The Methods say the study was conducted February-March 2019, but also describe a 10-day catch-and-effort protocol over four months; the Table 5 caption again says February-March 2019. The actual field window is unresolved.
studyScope.methodsSummary: Household surveys and a gear census were combined with structured catch-and-effort monitoring at pre-designated landing sites. The authors say representative fish specimens were transferred to the University Museum at the University of the Philippines for preservation, cataloging, and archiving.

reviewedFindings.habitatDescription: The authors describe all 14 catch species as reef-associated and relate the fishery to shallow reef-flat habitats.
reviewedFindings.proseExampleContext: These are the three dominant taxa named in the article's prose for the two gear variants; they are not copied into Bangwit's species or occurrence data.
reviewedFindings.siteResolution: Coverage is described across five municipalities, but the reviewed article does not provide a verified coordinate or a municipality-by-taxon occurrence crosswalk.
reviewedFindings.voucherStatus: The article reports transfer of specimens to the University Museum for cataloging, but the reviewed public text provides no voucher catalog numbers or specimen-level crosswalk.

qualityAndReuseLimits: This is a gear-selective catch assessment, not a complete Batanes marine fish checklist, a survey of all habitats, or freshwater evidence.
The February-March 2019 statement conflicts with the four-month monitoring description and figure/table captions; do not assign a precise sample date range until the authors clarify it.
The five municipality names do not locate individual sampling events, taxa, landing sites, or specimens. Do not infer coordinates or municipal-water geometry from the illustrative map.
Although the article says specimens were archived at the University Museum, no accession or voucher identifiers were verified in the reviewed material.

The article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Do not reproduce or adapt its species table, figures, or other protected material; check the license and any third-party credits before any proposed reuse. Publication approval remains false.
The article's claims about fishery efficiency, sustainability, or local norms are study-specific interpretations, not independently validated stock, safety, legal, or fishing-advice conclusions.
nextAction: Ask the authors or museum whether specimen catalog numbers, exact field dates, landing-site-to-municipality and taxon crosswalks, and any additional reuse permission are available. Keep this marine gear study separate from the unresolved Batanes freshwater-lake and river evidence queue.
